name: Indonesia
summary_text: Indonesia is a dangerous destination for trans visitors — with a directly documented trans-traveler death in custody and a presidential decree classifying LGBTQ+ as a national security threat. Rodrigo Ventocilla, a Harvard trans activist from Peru, died in Bali police custody in 2022 after arrest at Bali airport on his honeymoon (family alleges police beating; police deny violence). In Aceh province, Sharia law criminalises same-sex relations with public caning (applies to all persons in Aceh, including tourists). A new penal code effective January 2026 effectively criminalises all same-sex conduct nationally. President Prabowo in October 2025 classified "promotion of LGBTQ+ culture" as a national security threat alongside terrorism — and vigilante mob attacks on trans women escalated after this decree (10 attacks documented in Bogor between March and July 2026). Police conduct discriminatory raids on gay gatherings (75 arrested in Bogor in June 2025). BUT: Bali is a major tourist hub where many trans visitors enter discreetly without incident; Indonesia has no death penalty; and Rodrigo's death is disputed (police deny violence) rather than clearly documented state torture.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 401); the underlying Reuters report (Aug 2022) covers Indonesian police denying violence in the death of Harvard trans activist Rodrigo Ventocilla in Bali.

sources.title: ‘We Want to Clear Rodrigo’s Name’: Mother of Harvard Student who Died in Bali Says He was Beaten by Police | The Harvard Crimson
sources.claim_summary: Harvard Crimson (Sept 2022): the mother of Rodrigo Ventocilla Ventosilla - a 32-year-old Peruvian trans man and Harvard student - alleges he was arrested at Bali airport on drug charges, subjected to extortion (demands rising from $100,000 to $200,000), and died three days later in hospital while in police custody during his honeymoon.

sources.title: Indonesia’s Transgender Community Is Facing Growing Repression – The Diplomat
sources.claim_summary: The Diplomat (Aug 2026): Indonesia's transgender community faces growing repression - vigilante mobs attacking trans people as the government takes steps to codify anti-LGBT provisions.

sources.title: Attacks on trans women in Indonesia did not suddenly appear. Here's what's behind them - ABC News
sources.claim_summary: ABC News (Aug 2026): analysis of attacks on trans women in Indonesia after a rule deemed them a 'threat' - trans women who were previously able to appear in public have become afraid; the attacks did not appear suddenly but build on longer trends.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 401); the underlying Reuters report (Feb 2025) covers Aceh province publicly caning two men for a same-sex relationship.

sources.title: Indonesia | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): the new penal code in force from 2 January 2026 penalises all consensual extra-marital sex (2 years), effectively criminalising same-sex relations since marriage is unavailable (complaint-based enforcement); the vague 2016 National Pornography Act has been used to target LGBTIQ people - 2025 police raids on 'gay parties' detained 56 in Jakarta, 75 in Bogor, 34 in Surabaya; online LGBTIQ content blocked.
Human Dignity Trust country profile: two provinces of Indonesia (Aceh and South Sumatra) criminalise same-sex sexual activity between men and between women; national-level provisions target morality.

sources.title: Indonesia: Police must release 75 people arrested in discriminatory raid on “gay party” - Amnesty International
sources.claim_summary: Amnesty International (June 2025): police raided a privately rented villa in Bogor described as a 'gay party', arresting 75 people (74 men, 1 woman); Amnesty called it 'a blatant violation of human rights and privacy that exemplifies the hostile environment for LGBTI people in Indonesia' and demanded release and accountability.

sources.title: Indonesia: Surge in Abuse Against LGBT Students | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Jul 2026): 'Indonesia: Surge in Abuse Against LGBT Students' — documented surge in abuse of LGBT students by authorities and institutions amid criminal-code expansion and campus purges.

sources.title: “These Political Games Ruin Our Lives”: Indonesia’s LGBT Community Under Threat | HRW
sources.claim_summary: HRW report (Aug 2016) 'These Political Games Ruin Our Lives': Indonesia's LGBT community under threat - 70 interviews; documents the anti-LGBT cascade starting with the higher-education minister's campus ban call, the defense minister calling LGBT activism 'more dangerous than a nuclear bomb', and resulting legislative proposals threatening LGBT Indonesians' rights and safety.
